chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from one of our companions, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all together, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from his father, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said:

Al-Mahdi asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about wine, 'Is it prohibited in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic? For the people only know the prohibition (prevention) from it, and do not know its specific prohibition (haram status).'
So Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Yes, it is prohibited in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, O Commander of the Faithful.'
He said to him, 'In which place is it prohibited in the Book of Allah, Majestic is His Name, O Abu al-Hasan?'

He said, 'The Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: Say: Indeed, my Lord has only prohibited the immoralities, what is apparent of them and what is concealed, and the sin and the rebellion without right.'
As for His Words 'what is apparent of them', it means open adultery, and the raising of flags which the promiscuous women used to raise for their immorality in the Pre-Islamic period.

And as for His Words, Mighty and Majestic, 'and what is concealed', it means what the fathers married (i.e., the son marrying the father's wife), because the people, before the Prophet was sent (peace be upon him and his family), when a man had a wife and he died, his son would marry her after him, if she was not his mother. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prohibited that.

And as for 'the sin', it is the wine itself. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said in another place: 'They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: In both of them is a great sin and benefits for the people.'
As for the sin in the Book of Allah, it is the wine and the gambling, and their sin is greater, as Allah, the Exalted, has said.

He said, 'So Al-Mahdi said, 'O Ali ibn Yaqteen! By Allah, these are Hashimite fatwas.' I said to him, 'You speak the truth, by Allah, O Commander of the Faithful! Praise is for Allah, Who did not remove this knowledge from you, the People of the House.' He said, 'By Allah, Al-Mahdi could not be patient and said to me, 'You speak the truth, O Rafidi (Rejector).'

key_terms.هَاشِمِيَّةٌ: Of the Hashemites (referring to the Ahl al-Bayt lineage)

ai.seo_question: Where is wine prohibited in the Quran according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Imam's exegetical method of deriving specific legal rulings (Ahkam) from general Quranic terms, a cornerstone of Shia Usul al-Fiqh. By linking 'the sin' (ithm) in Surah Al-Baqarah directly to wine, the Imam establishes a definitive scriptural basis for prohibition beyond mere consensus, reinforcing the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt in interpreting divine text. Al-Mahdi’s acknowledgment of these as 'Hashimite fatwas' underscores the unique scholarly lineage and distinct interpretive authority of the Imams within the Shia tradition.
